title: Fordice v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s denial, and remanded for further proceedings. It rejected the claim that using BCO 38-1 instead of trial was itself error, but held that the approved statement and confession failed to address the underlying allegations fully and specifically.
first_summary: A church member challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaint after it resolved accusations against a minister through a BCO 38-1 confession rather than trial. The SJC sustained the complaint because the statement of facts and confession did not adequately address the specific allegations. It annulled the denial and remanded for Presbytery to amend the documents, institute process, reactivate the investigative committee, or otherwise respond directly to the unresolved allegations.
summary: A church member challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaint after it resolved accusations against a minister through a BCO 38-1 confession rather than trial. The SJC held that using confession without process was not itself error, but the statement and confession failed to correlate with and address the specific allegations. It sustained the complaint, annulled the denial, and remanded for Presbytery to amend the documents, institute process, reactivate the investigative committee, or otherwise respond directly and specifically to the unresolved allegations.

sources.supports: Issue, judgment, issue-level rulings, decisive reasoning, annulment, and remand instructions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case number and title appear at lines 13–17; the SJC unanimously approved the Panel’s proposed decision at lines 244–248 (printed pp. 532, 541–542).
evidence_notes.dispute: Fordice challenged Presbytery’s denial after its acceptance of a statement of facts and confession under BCO 38-1; lines 67–83 and 87–89 (printed pp. 535–536).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Use of BCO 38-1 was not itself erroneous (lines 110–171); the statement was not full because it failed to correlate with the allegations (lines 173–197); denial was annulled and the matter remanded for a direct response to unresolved allegations (lines 228–242), printed pp. 536–541.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC did not decide whether the accusations were true, and trial was not mandatory merely because investigators found a strong presumption of guilt; lines 108, 134–171, 173–175 (printed pp. 536–538).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. Hutchinson, Ruff, and Lyons were cited as precedents within the SJC’s own reasoning; lines 147–169 and 205–230 (printed pp. 537–540).

source_limits: The supplied source contains the operative judgment and reasoning but not the full underlying statement, confession, complaint, or investigative report.

verification_notes: Rechecked the judgment at lines 81–83 and final order at lines 240–244. The final summary clarifies that BCO 38-1 was not inherently improper and identifies inadequate correlation with the allegations—not avoidance of trial—as the decisive error.
